title: E-Scooter Trips in Minneapolis: What do they say about micromobility & transit access?
abstract: This project  uses scooter trip records and transit stop data in Minneapolis to ask whether scooters are mostly connecting people to transit (first/last mile) or substituting for transit (sub_one / sub_multi), and where they appear to fill access gaps beyond walking distance of bus stops.
introduction: How do shifts in racial and ethnic population demographics correlate with income changes across Minnesota counties over the past decade? We aimed to explore how economic gaps among racial and ethnic groups might affect income levels and access to economic opportunities. By doing so, we hope to highlight economic challenges faced by diverse communities and provide insights for policies that promote inclusion and equity.
shiny_output: Introduction Tab - An animated GIF showing changes in per capita income per county over time.
County-level Analysis Tab - Interactive county map with income and racial changes from 2012–2022. Slider for controlling visualization pace.
Tract-level Analysis Tab - Similar to county-level, but at census tract scale.
Income Trend Plot - Grey lines for all counties, highlighted blue line for the selected county.
Racial Makeup Trend Plot - Trends in racial composition for the selected county.
conclusions: 2019–2020 jump in income likely related to post-COVID economic rebound.
Counties with higher per capita income showed less fluctuation in racial composition.
Overall per capita income rose since 2012, but declined in 2021–2022, possibly due to inflation and tighter monetary policy.
Racial makeup generally increased across all groups, with exceptions like Renville County’s slight drop in Asian population.
further_research: Role of job availability and sector-specific income growth in shaping income disparities.
ethical_considerations: Census data is anonymous to protect privacy.
Our reporting avoids targeting any group and aims for bias-free observations.
We acknowledge potential census errors and keep interpretations cautious.
